prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In a downward-looking overhead scene (~0.5–1.0 m above a flat concrete floor), the depth map separates the dark, farthest floor surface (~0.8–1.0 m away) from two seated people who are roughly 0.1–0.3 m apart and well within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and each other. In frames 1–4, the person in green at the top-center/right is brightest and nearest (~0.4–0.6 m from the camera) with hands reaching down toward the floor, while the person in red on the left (with a henna-patterned lower arm at the bottom-left) sits at an intermediate depth (~0.6–0.8 m); both people's upper torsos and heads are out of view above/left of the frame, so neither is seen looking toward the camera wearer. In frame 5, as the camera pitches and shifts rightward/upward, the left person's draped knee and lower arm become the brightest, nearest surfaces (~0.4–0.5 m) while the top-right person appears slightly farther (~0.6–0.7 m) and partially shifts toward the upper-right edge. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly reveals the 3D vertical relief of the folded knees, draped clothing, and raised wrists above the floor plane. However, it is unreliable for small floor-level objects—smoothing over the white cotton wad, henna cones, and partially occluded smartphone—and suffers from relative scale rescaling across frames that makes the left person's knee abruptly flip from mid-gray to bright white between frames 2–3 and 4–5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map attempts to isolate the two close-range people (roughly 0.5–0.8 m from the camera wearer and 0.1–0.3 m from each other, both within arm's reach) against the unlabelled background floor, while their heads and upper bodies remain cropped out of view so gaze direction is not visible. In frame 2, it separates the scene into a brown mask on the left person (red garment, facing generally rightward/inward) and a pink mask on the top-center person (green garment, angled downward/leftward toward the floor space between them). Across the 5-frame sequence, however, the map fails to track consistent boundaries as the camera shifts in frame 5: frames 1 and 3 only segment the top-center person, frame 4 splits that same person into overlapping brown and pink masks while missing the left person, and frame 5 merges the left person's red skirt and yellow knee into a single perforated pink mask while missing the top-right person entirely. While segmentation in frame 2 helps delineate the boundary where the left person's arm meets the top person's torso and legs, it provides no labels at all for the small reachable items on the floor (two henna cones, cotton wad, and smartphone tucked under the top person's foot/leg). Overall, the map is highly unreliable, consistently omitting the henna-covered forearm at the bottom-left and suffering from severe under-segmentation, over-segmentation, and instance flickering.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a single magenta right-hand skeleton in frames 2, 3, and 4 belonging to the top-center person's right hand (~0.6–0.7 m below and in front of the camera wearer), with zero yellow body keypoints in any frame because both individuals' heads, shoulders, and upper torsos are occluded/cropped outside the field of view. This detected hand is positioned in the upper-left-center of the workspace, just to the right of the left person's red skirt (~0.05–0.1 m away) and ~0.1 m left of the same person's own left hand, holding a small cone within easy arm's reach of both people and the camera wearer. Across frames 2 to 4, the magenta finger keypoints curl inward and shift slightly downward toward the white cotton wad on the floor before disappearing in frame 5 when the hand moves upward and motion blur increases. Compared to the RGB strip, the skeleton clarifies the exact articulation and downward-pinching orientation of the fingers around the small cone despite dim shadows between the two people's legs. Nevertheless, the pose estimator is largely unreliable here, missing all body/limb joints for both people, failing to detect any hands in frames 1 and 5, and completely missing the top person's adjacent left hand and the left person's outstretched, henna-patterned forearm and hand at the bottom-left (~0.5–0.7 m from the camera).
